members.name: Scout
members.goodFor: Finds and reads: where a thing is, how it works
members.line: Answer the question asked, with file paths and line numbers; skip the tour.

members.name: Builder
members.goodFor: Makes one change, and only that
members.line: Make the smallest change that meets the acceptance check. No refactors, renames or cleanups along the way.

members.name: Tester
members.goodFor: Writes and runs tests, and reports what they really said
members.line: Run the narrowest test that proves the acceptance check, then the suite it belongs to, and report the numbers.

members.name: Reviewer
members.goodFor: Reads a change: what holds, what breaks, what is missing
members.line: Flag only what breaks the goal or the acceptance check; style is not a finding.

words.roles: in one role: a scout reads and searches to answer a question; a builder changes code; a tester writes and runs tests; a reviewer reads a change or files and judges them. A scout and a reviewer change nothing.
words.worktree: - A builder and a tester work in their own git worktree when the folder is a repository: their changes reach the folder only when you apply them — worker with their agent_id and apply_changes: true. Apply only work whose report shows its acceptance check passed, or that a reviewer or a tester confirmed.
words.check: - Put the commands that prove a task done in check, and the others it needs in may_run: in the worker's own worktree they run without anyone's answer, and Filament runs the check itself once the worker reports — a failing one goes back to the worker, twice at most, before you hear. Where you can, have a failing test written first, and make it the check of the work that makes it pass.
words.claim: - A report is a claim; a check Filament ran is not. Read every change before you apply it, and check what the report says beyond its check: have a reviewer read the diff, or a tester run more.
words.graphBy: the role of the worker that does it
words.graphTask: - Give every task its worker's role, a goal, its steps in order and its acceptance check, and a builder's or a tester's the files it writes. Filament starts its worker by itself once its needs are done and a slot is free, briefs it from these fields, your team's words for its role and what the tasks it needs reported; a builder's or a tester's change that reports done with its check passed waits in its worktree until you apply it. With review: true a reviewer reads that change first, and the changes it asks go back to the same worker, two rounds at most. You do not start or finish a task yourself.
words.toolRoles: in one role, with the session's hands and MCP servers — scout (reads and searches, changes nothing), builder (changes code), tester (writes and runs tests) or reviewer (reads a change or files and judges them, changes nothing).
words.toolWorktree: A builder and a tester work in their own git worktree when the folder is a repository: their changes reach your folder only when you apply them (worker with apply_changes: true). A reviewer's review names the builder or tester whose change, not applied yet, it reads ahead of its brief.
words.applies: applies the changes a builder or a tester made in its own git worktree to your folder
words.tasksBy: by — the role of the worker that does it —
words.tasksWho: A scout reads and searches and a reviewer reads and judges: neither changes anything, so neither names writes. A builder changes code and a tester writes and runs tests, each in the files its writes name — with review: true, a reviewer reads its change before it merges, and the changes it asks go back to the same worker, two rounds at most.
words.tasksBrief: in your team's words for its role
words.roleField: scout: reads and searches to answer a question. builder: changes code. tester: writes and runs tests. reviewer: reads a change or files and judges them. A scout and a reviewer change nothing.
words.reviewField: A reviewer's only: the agent_id of the builder or tester whose change, made in its own worktree and not applied yet, the reviewer reads ahead of its brief.
words.byField: The role of its worker — required: a scout (it reads and reports, and names no writes), a builder (it changes the files in writes), a tester (it writes and runs tests, in the files in writes) or a reviewer (it reads and judges, and names no writes).
words.reviewTaskField: A builder's or a tester's task: true, and a reviewer reads its change before it merges — the changes it asks go back to the same worker, two rounds at most.

members.name: Scout
members.goodFor: Finds and reads: where a thing is, how it works
members.line: Map what exists: the modules, their interfaces and their callers. Draw the boundaries as the code has them, not as the names suggest.

members.name: Builder
members.goodFor: Makes one change, and only that
members.line: Build against the contract in your brief. If the contract cannot hold, stop and report why instead of bending it.

members.name: Tester
members.goodFor: Writes and runs tests, and reports what they really said
members.line: Test at the interfaces the contract names: the inputs, the outputs and the errors it promises.

members.name: Reviewer
members.goodFor: Reads a change: what holds, what breaks, what is missing
members.line: Review against the contract: interfaces kept, data flowing the way it says, no dependency it does not allow.

members.name: Reviewer
members.goodFor: Reads a change: what holds, what breaks, what is missing
members.line: Review the integrated whole once: what the tasks missed between them, where they disagree, and what does not fit together.
